rationale: Food preservation for property and maintaining a closed fridge door for the household are related but not mutually identical responsibilities.
Midday oven readiness and evening kitchen readiness are distinct time-bound cooking contexts; the latter also covers a broader evening kitchen state.
Both maintain the resident's timely morning waking; weekday timing, alarm condition, shutters, and coffee machine are implementation or schedule variants.
Both address reliable timely morning waking; alarm response and gradual versus immediate actuators do not change the responsibility identity.
Both achieve waking at the intended morning time; exact seven o'clock scheduling and alarm actuation are configuration variants.
Turning off an unwatched TV is narrower than managing energy in a vacated living room, which also covers lighting and room departure.
Unwatched-TV energy control and unoccupied-bathroom boiler/fan control apply to materially different spaces and managed loads.
TV inactivity control and whole living-room energy reduction have different scope and managed outcomes, despite shared energy-saving intent.
Unwatched-TV shutdown is distinct from whole-home unoccupied energy saving that also activates cleaning and controls lights.
Scheduled automatic feeding and owner-triggered feeding when the dog is hungry are different care contexts and failure conditions.
Both maintain comfortable indoor temperature for a resident while occupied; heating versus cooling and thresholds are actuator/configuration variants.
Both provide resident awareness of a visitor at the door while away; phone frame versus intercom video/message is a notification-channel variant.
Both support reliable waking when an alarm is not dismissed; gradual lighting/shutter motion is an implementation variant.
Both support waking at the scheduled morning time; alarm dismissal contingency versus fixed seven o'clock alarm is a trigger/schedule variant.
Entrance lighting conservation and kitchen lighting conservation are room-specific responsibilities, so neither substitutes for the other.
A room-specific entrance-light duty is not interchangeable with ensuring all house lights are off when the entire house is empty.
Stopping power after full charge and shutting down idle devices have distinct guarded conditions and device-use outcomes.
Both guard home security while unoccupied; the listed locks, shutters, alarms, cameras, and notifications are concrete control variants.
Both support resident medication intake; morning versus evening timing and smartphone versus voice reminders are schedule/channel variants.
Both support timely resident waking; daylight blinds versus rising/vibrating bed are implementation actions for the same outcome.
Both maintain plant hydration; soil thresholds, pots, sprinklers, and notifications are configuration or implementation variants.
Living-room TV/light energy control and bathroom boiler/fan energy control are distinct room-specific responsibilities.
Both concern a living room but one is a room-departure duty while the other manages a broader unused-room state including a background display.
Living-room departure control is narrower than saving energy across an unoccupied home while also activating cleaning.
Bathroom boiler/fan conservation and unused living-room light/TV conservation are materially different room contexts and managed outcomes.
Bathroom-specific energy control is not interchangeable with broad unoccupied-home energy saving involving cleaning and lights.
